senses.gloss: (denom. of הֲנָאָה), Nif. נֶהֱנֶה (= נֵאוֹת, v. אוֹת I)
to be pleased, to enjoy, to profit.
units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 20a">B. Kam. 20ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>זה נה׳</he> the one is benefitted &c., opp. <cite ref="H01413"><he>חָסֵר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 2:2">Ib. II, 2</cite> <he>משלם מה שנֶהֱנֵית</he> he must pay for what the animal has enjoyed (eaten or drunk), contrad. to <he>מה שהזיקה</he> what she has damaged.

<cite ref="Berakhot 10b:21">Ber. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>הרוצה לֵהָנוֹת יהָנֶה וכ׳</he> (Rashi <he>לֵיהָ׳</he>) he who desires to make use (of people’s hospitalities), may do so following the example of Elisha.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 28a">R. Hash. 28ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מצות לא ליהנות ניתנו</he> religious ceremonies are not considered an enjoyment (as regards the use of sacred property &c.); a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Berakhot 35a:9">Ber. 35ᵃ</cite> <he>דבר שנ׳</he> something which is enjoyable (can be eaten &c.).

senses.gloss: to benefit, to entertain, to cause to share.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 92a:16">Snh. 92ᵃ</cite> <he>אינו מְהַנֶּה ת״ח וכ׳</he> allows no scholar to share his wealth.
<cite ref="Berakhot 63b:21">Ber. 63ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>ומְהַנֵּהוּ וכ׳</he> and invites him to partake of his wealth.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yadayim 4:3">Yad. IV, 3</cite> <he>הרי אתה כמְהַנָּן וכ׳</he> you appear to benefit them pecuniarily, but &c.
